sources.name: Town of Frederick: Frederick Events Calendar
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. CivicPlus, like Lyons, Berthoud, Erie and Johnstown. The Town keeps two public calendars; this is "Frederick Events Calendar" (CID 34), the Town-run community events: 2 items on 5 October (Frights on Fifth, 17 October, Downtown Frederick; Festival of Lights, 5 December, Crist Park, 105 Fifth Street), both all-day in the feed where the event pages give times. The iCal reaches further than the CivicPlus RSS (RSSFeed.aspx?ModID=58&CID=34, 1 item, current month only). The Town's signature events (Miners Day in September, Frederick in Flight in June, Chainsaws & Chuckwagons in July, Music in the Park on summer second Wednesdays, the Memorial Day ceremony) each have a page under /234/Events and reach the calendar only as the date nears, so the events page is read by hand as well. www.frederickco.gov/robots.txt is a Cloudflare content-signals stub with no rules; frederickco.gov's (CivicPlus) disallows /RSS.aspx and /CurrentEvents*.aspx, neither of which this reads. America/Denver times. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's. robots: subscribe from 29 October 2026, the editor's call delegated by the owner: CivicPlus added `Disallow: /common/modules/icalendar/` to every site it hosts on 20-21 October, which the check now reads case-blind, and this feed is the one the site offers residents as a calendar subscription; one nightly read is what a subscribed calendar does (DECISIONS.md, "CivicPlus's calendar feeds").

sources.name: Town of Frederick: Frederick Meetings Calendar
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. The Town's second public calendar (CID 38): 77 items to December 2030 on 5 October, every one a board or commission meeting (Board of Trustees regular and work sessions, Planning Commission, Parks, Recreation, Open Space & Trails Commission, Historic Preservation Committee, Frederick Arts Committee, Youth Commission, Urban Renewal Authority), with no LOCATION. The two titles excluded are the calendar's own placeholders ("One Time Event" on 31 December 2030, "Parking Lot for Agenda Items" on 30 December 2027), not meetings. Under the event standard (docs/archive/AUDIT-2026-10-02.md) routine meetings are not events; whether to confirm this feed at all, or exclude the regular sessions as Longmont's registry does, is the editor's call. The Town's nine other iCal categories (Centennial Park, Crist Park, Frederick Recreation Area, Downtown Activities, each board on its own) were each read once and are empty. Left proposed 5 October 2026: every item is a routine meeting, which the event standard excludes; confirm it only to have the meetings staged. Confirmed 6 October 2026 at the owner’s direction (an official Town calendar). Its routine board and commission meetings are excluded by title under the event standard, as Firestone’s and Dacono’s are, so it stages only what is not a regular meeting; remove an exclusion to have that body’s meetings staged. robots: subscribe from 29 October 2026, the editor's call delegated by the owner: CivicPlus added `Disallow: /common/modules/icalendar/` to every site it hosts on 20-21 October, which the check now reads case-blind, and this feed is the one the site offers residents as a calendar subscription; one nightly read is what a subscribed calendar does (DECISIONS.md, "CivicPlus's calendar feeds").

sources.name: Weld County: events listing
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. Granicus OpenCities (weldgov.com redirects here). The county's events listing filters by location, with Dacono, Firestone and Frederick each a choice, but only through an ASP.NET form post, and neither it, the County Calendar nor an event's own page offers iCal, RSS or JSON. Its 614-line robots.txt disallows several of the sub-calendars (holiday closures, the Health and Environment calendar, the commissioners' hearings calendar, job-seeker events) and allows the listing and the County Calendar. On 5 October the first page (5 to 15 October) had nothing in the three towns. Core as Boulder County is for Niwot and Lyons, but read by a person who sets the location filter; the county's offices and fairgrounds are in Greeley, thirty miles off. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's.

sources.name: Carbon Valley Chamber of Commerce
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026: not readable. Every path on carbonvalleychamber.com, robots.txt included, answers automated requests with HTTP 202 and a SiteGround captcha page, so neither the site's robots rules nor its calendar could be read, and its CMS is unknown; the old GrowthZone calendar at business.carbonvalleychamber.com answers 410 Gone. The chamber is real (Firestone's History page and the Carbon Valley Parks and Recreation District both name it; CVPRD lists its Chamber Open golf tournament on 17 August). The host name is the obvious one and was not confirmed from an official page. Read by a person in a browser, or ask the chamber for its calendar. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's. A manual source: confirming it puts it on the weekly check, where it will report blocked until the chamber's site admits readers.

sources.name: Carbon Valley Regional Library (High Plains Library District), LibCal
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. One branch serves all three towns: 7 Park Avenue, Firestone (Mon to Thu 9 am to 8 pm, Fri and Sat 10 am to 5 pm, Sun 1 to 5 pm, per mylibrary.us/locations-and-hours/). The district's LibCal is the same one the Windsor and Johnstown work found: its public iCal (ical_subscribe.php?src=p&cid=8181) is the district's 500 oldest items, 4 August to 25 September 2026 on 5 October, and no parameter (cal, cm, inc, d, t) narrows it to the branch or moves it forward, re-tested three ways. The district-wide RSS (rss.php?iid=4057&m=month&cid=8181; m=upcoming answers "invalid mode") does carry the coming fortnight, 300 items on 5 October of which 19 were at the Carbon Valley Regional Library (Drop-in Chess, English Class, Tween Craft Club, Sketch Club, Page Turner's Book Club), but its dates, times and building are inside each item's description, which the repo's RSS reader does not read (it reads CivicPlus's calendarEvent elements), so ingest would stage nothing from it: reading LibCal RSS would be a new feed reader, which is a feature to ask about. Until then the branch's calendar page, linked above with the building preselected, is read in a browser. robots.txt names a 10-second crawl delay for everyone and disallows the /process_ endpoints the page loads events from, so the page cannot be read by script either. The locationFilter is set for the day a reader exists. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's. Read as RSS from 5 October 2026: scripts/lib/feeds/rss.ts now reads LibCal's own libcal:date, libcal:time, libcal:location and libcal:campus elements (the district-wide feed covers the coming fortnight or so, 300 items on 5 October), and the locationFilter keeps the branch's. Exclusions set 5 October 2026 from the event standard in docs/archive/AUDIT-2026-10-02.md (routine meetings, the court and office closures are not events), at the owner's direction that the sources be settled on the editor's judgment; remove any to have it staged again. Storytimes, clubs, drop-ins, the English class and the advisory board are excluded; what remains is the one-off programs (a science afternoon, a teen improv session, an adult D&D one-shot, a 3D-modelling class). The feed marks a called-off session by prefixing "Cancelled:" to the title, as Longmont's does. The branch is in Firestone, so staged items carry subTown firestone. Excluded on 5 October 2026 at the review: "Let’s Draw!" and "Science Fun", monthly after-school sessions for elementary pupils (a class in all but name, under the event standard). "Ageless Grace" was already excluded; its cancelled session reached staging because the feed wrote a non-breaking space in the title, which the readers now treat as a space. Feed narrowed on 5 October 2026 to the branch with cam=4554 (the calendar's own building filter): 62 items, all at Carbon Valley, reaching about a month ahead where the district feed's 300 reach a fortnight. The locationFilter stays as a guard. Further exclusions on 5 October 2026, with the branch feed: the baby storytime (Twinkle Babies), the job-help drop-in, the legal clinic, Library 101, the monthly Paws to Read, make-and-take craft classes (Cricut, tote bags, looming), as Longmont excludes them, and the bird walk at Golden Ponds, which is in Longmont. Moved to the Frederick guide on 2 November 2026 when Carbon Valley closed: the branch is at 7 Park Avenue in Firestone and is the Frederick area's library (High Plains Library District), so its programs are listed where a Frederick family would look for them.

sources.name: Carbon Valley Parks and Recreation District
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. The special district (established 1983, 45 square miles: Dacono, Firestone, Frederick and the country between) that runs the Carbon Valley Recreation Center, 701 Fifth Street, Frederick, the Community (Active Adults) Center and the Gymnastics Center, and the recreation programming for all three towns. Streamline (CivicPlus) site with no events module, no calendar page and no feed; the Special Events page is a hand-written list ("2026 Schedule of Events": Carbon Valley Kids Day 6 June in Firestone, Boot Scoot'n Bash 12 June in Dacono, the Chamber Open 17 August, Miners Day 19 September in Frederick, Zumba Glow Party 16 October, Eye of Freedom Encounter 28 October, Harvest & Holly Market 15 November 11 am to 3 pm at the Recreation Center, Burn the Bird Fitness Party 27 November) and the Active Adults page another (Senior Resource Fair, Empty Bowls Painting Party 12 October). Programs register through CivicRec (secure.rec1.com), which has no feed. The monthly Rec Connect newsletter PDF (/rec-connect-newsletter) is the fullest schedule. robots.txt allows everything but the SEO bots. Read by hand; each event's subTown is where it is held, not the district. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's.

sources.name: Town of Frederick: Parks, Open Space and Trails
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026. The Town's Parks, Open Space and Trails Division (Town-owned parks, open space, trails) and Golf Division (Bella Rosa Golf Course, the Frederick Recreation Area). No calendar of its own: park events go on the Frederick Events Calendar above, and recreation programming for Frederick is the Carbon Valley Parks and Recreation District's (cvprd-com). The facilities directory lists the parks (Centennial Park, 630 Eighth Street; Crist Park, 105 Fifth Street; Coalridge, Confluence, Countryside, Bulrush Open Space, the skate park at the Frederick Recreation Area); its later pages load by script, so read it in a browser. Confirmed 5 October 2026 on the owner's word that the choice was the editor's.

sources.name: Longmont Leader

Site-wide RSS at /rss (20 items a page, paginated) and an Events section feed at /rss/colorado/events (20 items, press-release style); neither mentioned Frederick, Firestone, Dacono or Carbon Valley on 5 October, and a news feed carries no event dates for ingest to read. For the editor's reading, not the pipeline.

sources.name: Longmont Times-Call: Carbon Valley tag
sources.notes: Found and read once on 5 October 2026, by hand only. The paper covers the three towns under a Carbon Valley tag (4 October: "Dacono cancels City Council election, reelects two members"; "Colo. 52 to close for construction east of I-25"). Its main feed (/feed/) answers our user agent 403, which the repo treats as a site that blocks automated reads, and its robots.txt header forbids text and data mining and commercial reuse; the tag feed happened to answer 200 in the same batch and is not used. Link, never fetch. The Greeley Tribune (Weld County's paper) answered the same way.
